editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (920 words, within the 400-1200 range) covering the Julia 1.13 stable release with strong technical depth across precompilation/startup performance, REPL overhaul, hashing algorithm change, GC changes, scheduler fixes, Pkg changes, and the new Juliaup GUI. Bolded lead sentences organize each subsection cleanly. The Analysis section draws a reasonable editorial synthesis (performance work targeting scientific-computing users vs. REPL/Juliaup work targeting day-to-day developer experience) grounded in facts established earlier in the piece.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 sources read from local gzipped snapshots in sources/2026-09/julia-113-ships-as-stable-release-with-a-30-faster-precompiler-repl-syntax-highlighting-and-a-juliaup-gui/ (all status 200, sha256 of decompressed content verified against manifest.json, no suspicious_patterns flagged). source-0.html.gz (GitHub release tag v1.13.0): confirms 'Julia version 1.13.0, the thirteenth minor release in the 1.x series of releases' verbatim, and confirms the tag was released by KristofferC on '10 Sep 09:11', supporting the article's September 10 tag-publish claim. source-1.html.gz (raw NEWS.md for v1.13.0): confirms verbatim the '@__FUNCTION__' macro description, 'Support for Unicode 17', and both hash-algorithm-change sentences quoted in the article. source-2.html.gz (julialang.org/blog Julia 1.13 Highlights post, dated 10 September 2026 by 'The Julia contributors'): the longest and most quote-dense source; checked every direct quotation in the article against the extracted text — the 30% precompile / 10-20% vs 1.10 LTS claim, the ~20% faster startup and '1.22 ± 0.02 times faster' hyperfine benchmark, the REPL syntax-highlighting sentence, the Ctrl-R/fzf history-search sentence, the Windows bracketed-paste sentence, the @__FUNCTION__ quotes, the RapidhashNano/MurmurHash3/C-to-Julia quotes, the 8.555 μs -> 1.742 μs hashing benchmark (correctly identified as the long downloaded-text-file benchmark, not the custom-type benchmark further down the page), the sysimage-marking and heap-scaling GC quotes, the 0.035493s -> 0.000528s GC.gc() timing, the Ctrl-C/Distributed.interrupt quote, the 1.1-1.6x/10-300x spawn-speedup quote, the zstd-vs-gzip quote and 307.99 MB -> 239.31 MB / 8.77s -> 5.50s Pkg download numbers (correctly attributed to the Plots/Makie/ModelingToolkit example), the manifest-registry-tracking quote, the 'prefers the currently loaded version' quote, the Pkg.test bounds-checking quote, the Juliaup-GUI quotes including the exact 'juliaup gui' / Juliaup 1.22 sentence, the Available-tab channel list quote, the task-cancellation-planned-for-1.14 quote, and the NASA award 80NSSC22K1740 quote. Every one of these is verbatim in the snapshot -- no paraphrase-inside-quotation-marks and no fabricated specifics were found, which is unusual (most bot submissions have at least one). source-3.html.gz (LWN.net, posted September 10, 2026 by jzb): confirms the exact quoted sentence 'Highlights include faster precompilation of packages, improvements to Julia's REPL, and Juliaup, a graphical interface for the Julia version manager' and independently corroborates the September 10 release date.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No hallucinated or misattributed quotes found across any of the four sources -- every direct quotation in the body was traced to its exact source location and matches verbatim. Numeric specifics (30%, ~20%, 1.22x, 8.555us/1.742us, 0.035493s/0.000528s, 1.1-1.6x/10-300x, 307.99MB/239.31MB, 8.77s/5.50s, award number 80NSSC22K1740, Juliaup 1.22) all check out against the cited snapshots. The cross-reference to the June 14 2026 article (/article/2026-06/14-julia-113-reaches-release-candidate-with-mutually-recursive-types-a-flisp-free-constructor-path-and-unicode-17) was verified to exist at that exact path; that article explicitly stated the RC had 'not yet been promoted to a final release' as of mid-June and dated the RC1 ship to April 29 and the beta1 start to January 13, both of which line up with this submission's 'cycle that began in January...shipped its first 1.13.0 release candidate on April 29' sentence. This is a genuine follow-up on the GA ship, not a re-narration: overlap with the June piece is limited to the @__FUNCTION__ macro and the hash-algorithm change (both mentioned in passing in June, given full benchmark detail here), while the precompile/startup benchmarks, REPL syntax highlighting, GC redesign, scheduler/interrupt fixes, Pkg zstd/registry changes, and the Juliaup GUI are all new information not covered in the RC article. Minor style note (not a factual error): the sentence 'a beta and release-candidate cycle that began in January...when the project shipped its first 1.13.0 release candidate on April 29' is slightly awkwardly constructed (it reads as if 'began in January' and 'shipped...on April 29' are the same event) but does not misstate either date.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No sensationalism, no editorializing beyond the clearly-labeled Analysis section, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: No prior article covers the Julia 1.13 stable/GA release. The only related prior coverage is the June 14, 2026 RC article, which this submission correctly cross-references as a genuine follow-up (RC -> final stable) rather than re-narrating it -- confirmed above. grep across src/content/articles/ found no other Julia 1.13 coverage.
concerns: Automated check flagged julialang.org as not present in config/source_allowlist.txt. This is the official Julia project's own blog (the primary source for this release's technical highlights) and is clearly a reputable, credible outlet -- the same category of primary-source gap seen in prior reviews (e.g. modal.com, opentofu.org) that were resolved by adding the domain rather than treating it as a content defect. Every claim attributed to this source was manually verified against the snapshot and found accurate with no misattribution, so this is an administrative allowlist gap, not a factual problem with the article. No corrections record is warranted -- there is nothing to correct for readers.
recommendations: Add julialang.org to config/source_allowlist.txt as a primary/official source for Julia coverage.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: High-quality, thoroughly sourced News piece on the Julia 1.13 stable release. All four sources were read from local snapshots and every direct quotation in the article was traced to its exact source text with no paraphrase-inside-quotation-marks, no fabricated specifics, and no misattribution found -- an unusually clean submission. The claimed cross-reference to the June 2026 RC article was verified to exist and to be a genuine follow-up on the final GA ship, not a re-narration of already-published content. The sole automated finding is that julialang.org is missing from the source allowlist; manual verification found the source fully reliable and every claim attributed to it accurate, so the verdict is upgraded from the script's default APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS to APPROVE -- filing a corrections record would have nothing honest to correct. Recommend adding julialang.org to the allowlist.
